title: WPMS/726/2020 of KRISHAN KUMAR JAISWAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPMS No. 726 of 2020
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Arvind Vashisht, Senior
Advocate, assisted by Mr. Vivek Pathak,
Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. H.M. Raturi, Mr. Vinod Nautiyal,
Mr. T.S. Bisht, Deputy Advocate General,
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Mr. S.K. Mishra, Mr. R.C.
Arya, Mr. I.P. Kohli and Mr. Pradeep
Hariya, Standing Counsel, Mr. Atul
Bahuguna, Mr. M.S. Bisht, Mr. V.P.
Khanduri, Mr. Anirudh Bhatt, Mr. V.D.
Bisen, Mr. Gajendra Tripathi & Mr. V.S.
Rawat, Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
through video conferencing.
By means of this writ petition,
petitioner has sought following relief:
"(a) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari quashing the order
dated 03.02.2020 passed by S.D.M. Sadar
Dehradun as also quashing the inquiry
report dated 16.11.2019 submitted by 3
member committee consisting of Tehsildar,
Sadar, Dehradun, Nayab Tehsildar,
Dehradun and Revenue Sub Inspector,
Jakhan Dehradun."
As per the case set-up in the writ
petition, petitioner purchased agricultural
land comprised in Khasra Nos. 593, 610 &
608 situate in Village Gujrada Man Singh,
Pargana Parwadoon Tehsil & District
Dehradun by means of a registered sale
deed dated 28.02.2004. In para no. 6 of
the writ petition, it has been stated that
the entire property so purchased was
transferred by petitioner to one Mr. Jaswir
Singh, by means of registered sale deed
dated 30.05.2006. Thus, it can be safely

inferred that petitioner is left with no land
in the said village after 30.05.2006.
It transpires that a Public Interest
Litigation, being WPPIL No. 153 of 2018,
was filed by one Mr. Ravindra Singh Negi
seeking removal of encroachment from
Government land situated in Village
Gujrada Man Singh, Pargana Parwadoon
Tehsil & District Dehradun. A Division
Bench of this Court disposed of the said
WPPIL vide order dated 24.10.2018 with a
direction to District Magistrate, Dehradun
to ensure removal of encroachments from
Khasra No. 607 and 608 Kh situate in
Village Gujrara Mansingh, Pargana
Parwadoon Tehsil & District Dehradun
within a period of three months.
Pursuant to the direction issued in
the aforesaid PIL, a three member
committee was constituted to identify the
encroachment over the public land. The
said Inquiry Committee, headed by
Tehsildar, Sadar Dehradun, visited the
village on 29.09.2019 and identified the
encroachments made over Government
land.
The report of the Inquiry Committee
is on record as annexure no. 9 to the writ
petition, in which a finding was recorded
against petitioner that he transferred land
in excess of what was purchased by him.
Another finding has come in the inquiry
report that certain individuals, including
petitioner, have transferred Government
land to third persons. Based on the report
of Inquiry Committee, Sub Divisional
Magistrate, Sadar Dehradun passed an
order which, inter alia, provides for
cancellation of order of mutation passed in
favour of the petitioner regarding the land
purchased by him in the year 2004. Thus,

feeling aggrieved, petitioner has
approached this Court challenging the
report of Inquiry Committee and also the
order passed by S.D.M., Sadar Dehradun
on 03/07.02.2020.
Since the petitioner has transferred
the entire land purchased by him in the
said village and he has no right, title or
interest whatsoever left in respect of land
situate in the said village, therefore, in my
humble opinion, petitioner cannot be said
to be a person aggrieved by the order
dated 03/07.02.2020 passed by Sub
Divisional Magistrate, Sadar, Dehradun.
Only the subsequent purchasers, who are
presently having any right, title or interest
over the land in question, can maintain a
petition against the order passed by
S.D.M, Sadar, Dehradun on 03/
07.02.2020, if it adversely affects their
rights.
Even otherwise also, cancellation of
order of mutation will not divest the
rightful owner of his right or title over the
subject land.
It is settled position in law that
mutation of property in revenue records is
done for fiscal purpose and it does not
create or extinguish title over the land, nor
such entry has any presumptive value on
the title of such land.
In such view of the matter, the writ
petition is dismissed as not maintainable.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
Arpan 17.06.2020
